name: TCPDump — BPF Packet Filters & TCP Flag Hunting
description: TCPDump uses Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) syntax to filter captures by host, network, port, protocol, packet size, and logical operators. Filters can be applied pre-capture (drop non-matching traffic) or post-capture when reading a PCAP (non-destructive). TCP flag inspection requires byte-offset syntax: tcp[13] accesses the flags byte.
source: CDSA Module 07: Intro to Network Traffic Analysis
notes:
=== BPF FILTER SYNTAX ===
Filters can be applied:
  → Pre-capture: packets NOT matching are dropped (can lose evidence)
  → Post-capture: applied to PCAP file — view changes, file unchanged

=== HOST & NETWORK FILTERS ===
# Bidirectional host filter (src OR dst)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <IP>

# Source host only
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 src host <IP>

# Destination host only
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 dst host <IP>

# Source with port
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp src port 80

# Destination network (CIDR notation)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 dest net <NETWORK>/<CIDR>

# Source network
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 src net <NETWORK>/<CIDR>

=== PORT FILTERS ===
# Bidirectional port filter
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443

# Protocol + port (more specific than port alone)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp port 443

# DNS (uses both TCP and UDP)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 53

# Port range
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 portrange 0-1024

# NOT a port
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 not port 22

=== PROTOCOL FILTERS ===
# By protocol name
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 icmp
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 udp
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp

# By protocol number (IANA numbers)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 proto 6    # TCP = 6
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 proto 17   # UDP = 17
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 proto 1    # ICMP = 1

=== SIZE FILTERS ===
# Packets less than N bytes (shows SYN, FIN, KeepAlive, small ACKs)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 less 64

# Packets greater than N bytes (shows data payloads, file transfers)
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 greater 500

=== LOGICAL OPERATORS ===
# AND — both conditions must match
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <IP> and port 23
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 src host <IP> and tcp port 80

# OR — either condition matches
sudo tcpdump -r capture.pcap icmp or host <IP>

# NOT — exclude condition
sudo tcpdump -r capture.pcap not icmp
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 not port 22

# Combined: clear UDP+ARP, see only TCP
sudo tcpdump -r capture.pcap '!udp && !arp'

=== READING FROM FILE WITH FILTER ===
# Isolate DNS traffic from PCAP
sudo tcpdump -r capture.pcap udp and port 53

# Show only HTTP GET requests (needs -A or -X to see content)
sudo tcpdump -r capture.pcap -A tcp port 80

=== TCP FLAG HUNTING (BYTE OFFSET SYNTAX) ===
# TCP header byte 13 contains the flags
# Bit positions: URG=32, ACK=16, PSH=8, RST=4, SYN=2, FIN=1

# Capture packets with SYN flag set
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[13] &2 != 0'

# Capture ONLY SYN (not SYN-ACK)
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[13] == 2'

# Capture RST packets
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[13] &4 != 0'

# Capture FIN packets
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[13] &1 != 0'

# Capture packets with BOTH SYN and ACK (handshake response)
tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[13] == 18'

=== FILTER REFERENCE TABLE ===
Filter          | Effect
host x.x.x.x   | src OR dst matching host
src x.x.x.x    | source only
dst x.x.x.x    | destination only
net x.x.x.x/24 | src OR dst on this network
port 80         | src OR dst port
tcp port 443    | TCP only, port 443
portrange 0-1024| any port in range
less 64         | packets < 64 bytes
greater 500     | packets > 500 bytes
icmp/tcp/udp    | protocol name
proto 17        | protocol by IANA number
and / &&        | both must match
or / ||         | either matches
not / !         | negate condition
